candidates.name: Cable Silverback Shrug
candidates.cardText:
Cable Silverback Shrug
Novice
1
Use a bar attachment. Cable should be set all the way to the bottom.
2
Stand up with the attachment in hand, walk a couple of steps back make sure you are standing upright and not leaning backwards.
3
Retract your shoulder blades and then protract to return to the starting position.

candidates.name: Cable 30 Degree Shrug
candidates.cardText:
Cable 30 Degree Shrug
Beginner
1
Use a handle attachment on both sides of crossover. With cable attachment set all the way to the bottom.
2
Grab both handles and make sure you are centered in the machine. Let your arms hang freely.
3
Pull your shoulder blades up and in towards your ears. Let your shoulder blades depress back to the starting position.

candidates.name: Cable Upright Row
candidates.cardText:
Cable Upright Row
Advanced
1
Use a handle attachment with the cable set to the bottom of the machine.
2
Pull your elbows straight up toward the ceiling until the attachment is just below your chin then extend until your elbows are fully extended.

candidates.name: Cable Single Arm 30 Degree Shrug
candidates.cardText:
Cable Single Arm 30 Degree Shrug
Beginner
1
Use a handle attachment. With the cable attachment set all the way to the bottom.
2
Grab one handle and make sure you are centered in the machine. Let your arm hang freely.
3
Pull your shoulder blade up and in towards your ears. Let your shoulder blade depress back to the starting position.

candidates.name: Cable Rope Upright Row
candidates.cardText:
Cable Rope Upright Row
Beginner
1
Use a rope attachment with the cable set to the bottom of the machine.
2
Pull your elbows straight up toward the ceiling until the attachment is just below your chin then extend until your elbows are fully extended.

candidates.name: Cable Bilateral Cross Upright Row
candidates.cardText:
Cable Bilateral Cross Upright Row
Beginner
1
Stand between crossed low cables, holding the opposite handle in each hand.
2
Pull both handles upward, leading with your elbows.
3
Stop near chest height, then lower the handles slowly.
